stem: A 28-year-old man comes to the emergency department due to anxiety, weakness, dyspnea, and headaches.  He is a graduate student in chemistry and was accidentally exposed to nitrites in his research laboratory.  Physical examination is notable for cyanosis that is not improved by administration of supplemental oxygen via facemask.  Arterial blood drawn from this patient prior to any oxygen supplementation is most likely to reveal normal values for which of the following?​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​​​​‌​​​​​​‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌​‌​​‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌​‌‌​​​​‌‌​​​​‌‌​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​​​‌​‌‌‌‌​​​​‌‌​‌​‌‌​​​​‌​​‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌‌​​‌‌​​‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​​​​​‌‌​‌‌​‌​​‌‌​​‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​​​‌‌‌‌​‌‌​‌​​‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌​‌​‌‌​​​‌‌​​‌​​‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌​​‌‌‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​​‌​‌​​‌​​​‌‌‌​‌​​​​​​​​‌‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌​‌‌​​‌​‌‌

options.label: A
options.text: Bound fraction of oxygen in arterial blood

options.label: B
options.text: Oxygen carrying capacity of arterial blood

options.label: E
options.text: Partial pressure of oxygen in arterial blood

explanation:
Iron bound to heme is normally in the reduced ferrous (Fe2+) state.  Nitrites cause poisoning by inducing the conversion of this heme iron to the oxidized ferric (Fe3+) state, leading to the formation of methemoglobin.  With iron in the oxidized ferric state, methemoglobin is unable to bind oxygen.  In addition, the oxygen affinity of any residual ferrous iron in the hemoglobin tetramer is increased, causing a leftward shift of the oxygen-dissociation curve.  However, the partial pressure of oxygen in arterial blood (ie, the amount of oxygen dissolved in the plasma), is unchanged because pulmonary gas exchange remains normal.

Methemoglobinemia causes dusky discoloration of the skin (similar to cyanosis), and because methemoglobin is unable to carry oxygen, a state of functional anemia is induced.

(Choice A)  The bound fraction of oxygen refers to the percentage of O2 carried by hemoglobin versus that which is dissolved in plasma.  Because methemoglobin cannot bind O2, the proportion of oxygen carried bound to hemoglobin is decreased (not normal).

(Choices B and C)  Oxygen carrying capacity represents the maximum amount of O2 that blood can carry and is directly dependent on the amount of functional hemoglobin.  Because methemoglobin is non-functional, the blood's capacity to carry oxygen is decreased.  Oxygen content reflects the actual total amount of O2 in blood.  Since carrying capacity is reduced in this case, less O2 is bound to hemoglobin so total O2 content is also decreased.

(Choice D)  Oxygen delivery to the tissues is directly dependent on cardiac output and arterial O2 content.  Because O2 content of the blood is reduced with methemoglobinemia, delivery to tissues is decreased (causing this patient's weakness, headache, and dyspnea).

Educational objective:Methemoglobinemia causes dusky discoloration of the skin (similar to cyanosis), and because methemoglobin is unable to carry oxygen, a state of functional anemia is induced.  However, the blood partial pressure of oxygen in arterial blood is unchanged, as it is a measure of oxygen dissolved in plasma and is unrelated to hemoglobin function.​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​​​​‌​​​​​​‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌​‌​​‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌​‌‌​​​​‌‌​​​​‌‌​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​​​‌​‌‌‌‌​​​​‌‌​‌​‌‌​​​​‌​​‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌‌​​‌‌​​‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​​​​​‌‌​‌‌​‌​​‌‌​​‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​​​‌‌‌‌​‌‌​‌​​‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌​‌​‌‌​​​‌‌​​‌​​‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌​​‌‌‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​​‌​‌​​‌​​​‌‌‌​‌​​​​​​​​‌‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌​‌‌​​‌​‌‌
